description: Imports HubSpot CRM objects (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, line items, products, engagements), marketing assets (forms, form submissions, campaigns, email events, subscriptions, workflows), pipelines, owners, and any portal-defined custom objects.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment per endpoint; no global version header. The connector mixes CRM v3 (/crm/v3/...), CRM v4 associations (/crm/v4/...), properties v2 (/properties/v2/...), legacy v1 (/contacts/v1, /email/public/v1, /engagements/v1, /form-integrations/v1, /crm-pipelines/v1), marketing v3 and automation v3.

credentialModes.name: OAuth (bring your own HubSpot developer app + refresh token)

continuity.ourSideLoss: HubSpot's search endpoints cap any one query at 10,000 results and the recent-engagements endpoint at the 10,000 most recently modified engagements; the connector detects both caps and restarts the query from the newest cursor it reached, so a long pause plus a very high change rate can skip records between the cap and the restart point. Client-side-incremental streams (campaigns, forms, owners, workflows, pipelines, deals_archived) re-read the entire collection every run and lose nothing.
continuity.notes: Pure polling REST connector: it holds no server-side state in the customer's HubSpot portal (no webhook, subscription, or export job is created), so nothing accrues on their side while we are stopped. Resumption is driven entirely by the connector's own checkpointed cursor (updatedAt / hs_lastmodifieddate / timestamp), and HubSpot keeps history indefinitely, so an arbitrarily long pause is safe apart from the 10k caps noted above. Deletes are never observed — no stream reads an archived/deleted feed except deals_archived.

authTierRationale: Two modes are offered. The Private App mode needs exactly one self-serve value — an access token the admin copies out of their HubSpot portal's Private Apps page — sent as a bearer token, so it is T1_SIMPLE and sets the overall tier. The OAuth mode as written is T3_BYO_REFRESH standalone: the config demands client_id, client_secret AND refresh_token, and the connector refreshes against /oauth/v1/token itself. Estuary's hosted control plane hides that (spec.yaml carries x-oauth2-provider: hubspot and __main__.py supplies an OAuth2Spec whose accessTokenResponseMap writes /refresh_token into the config), so Estuary's own users only click through consent — but that relief comes from the control plane registering the app, not from the connector.

unionMisfits.description: IncrementalStream-based streams (contact_lists, email_events, subscription_changes, line_items, products, goals) do not send a single 'since' param. They send a PAIR of unix-MILLISECOND bounds, startTimestamp/endTimestamp, sliced into 30-day windows (or one window covering start_date..now when need_chunk is False). The schema's incrementalParam is a single {param, format} and its format enum has no millisecond option.

The search paginator has a hard ceiling: HubSpot rejects paging past 10,000 results for one query, so the connector stops at after >= 10000, checkpoints the highest cursor seen, and issues a NEW search starting from that cursor. The same trick is used for engagements (recent/modified caps at 10,000). This 'restart the query from the cursor' behaviour is a third pagination axis the Paginator union has no slot for.

restartAt.restartFrom: max cursor value emitted so far

unionMisfits.description: Every stream with an `entity` first calls GET /properties/v2/{entity}/properties to learn the portal's custom property names, then requests them explicitly. If the encoded property list exceeds 15000 characters the connector splits it into chunks and issues one request per chunk for the SAME page, merging the responses by primary key. v3 endpoints take one comma-joined `properties=` param; v1 endpoints take a repeated `property=` param. A PullSpec has no way to express 'fan out this page across N requests and merge'.

The CRM search endpoint cannot return associations, so after each search page the connector issues one extra POST per associated object type: POST /crm/v4/associations/{fromEntity}/{toEntity}/batch/read with body {"inputs": [{"id": ...}]} over the ids just fetched, and grafts the results onto the records. The backfill leg does not need this — it passes associations= on the object list call. A PullSpec models one request per page, not a page plus N enrichment calls.

enrichment.inputIds: ids of the records on the current page

unionMisfits.description: The campaigns list call is followed by one GET /email/public/v1/campaigns/{id} per row, and the emitted record is the merge of the list row and the detail response. Same page-plus-enrichment shape as above, but keyed per record rather than per page.

campaigns, deals_archived, deal_pipelines, ticket_pipelines, forms, form_submissions, owners and workflows have NO server-side filter. Each run re-reads the whole collection and drops records whose cursor is below the checkpoint in the connector. That is neither a real backfill/incremental split (the request is identical, which is why both legs carry the same PullSpec here) nor a `snapshot` (state does advance and output is filtered).

Classified as `cursor` with tokenFrom: body because the connector reads a value out of the response envelope ('offset' or 'vid-offset') and echoes it back in a query param — it does not compute offsets itself on this branch. The value happens to be a numeric offset (or a contact vid), which makes it look like an `offset` paginator even though the mechanism is envelope-token echoing. Note also the base class has a THIRD, client-computed fallback (offset += limit, terminate on short page) used only when the response body is a bare JSON array; no stream mined here takes that branch.

abstained.streams[15].pull.incremental.paginator.e: The class sets no more_key and the base next_page_token only paginates when the envelope carries 'paging' (v3) or the class's more_key (v1); this v1 crm-pipelines envelope has neither, so the connector reads exactly one page. Whether HubSpot itself would paginate this endpoint is not determinable from the repo.
abstained.streams[21].pull.incremental.paginator.t: The class sets no more_key, so the base next_page_token can only paginate this stream via the v3 'paging.next.after' branch (streams.py:704-706). No fixture in the repo exercises the form-integrations envelope, so the presence of that envelope is inferred from the code path, not observed.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: The connector performs one bounded sweep per invocation and exits; scheduling is imposed by the Flow runtime (estuary-cdk shim_airbyte_cdk drives delegate.read() once per open). Neither the connector nor its resource config declares an interval or cron.
abstained.streams[].schedules: No stream declares an interval or cron; the resource config exposes only stream/syncMode/cursorField/namespace.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: Set to 'merge' throughout because every binding declares a document key and Flow reduces on it, but the connector never emits deletion tombstones and no stream reads a deleted/archived feed except deals_archived, so hard deletes in HubSpot are invisible. If the reader's platform distinguishes keyed-upsert from append, treat property_history / subscription_changes / email_events (keyed by an event timestamp) as effectively append-only.
abstained.streams[goals]: goals is constructed in SourceHubspot.streams (source.py:110) but does NOT appear in the committed discover snapshot, presumably because the test portal lacks crm.objects.goals.read. Listed here from the code.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.params.limit: Page sizes are the connector's class defaults, not HubSpot maxima; several (e.g. count=1000 on /contacts/v1/lists) exceed the documented API maximum and are presumably clamped server-side.
